did_you_know.text: The LORD answers Job from the whirlwind—a description that emphasizes the power of the moment and the beginning of a direct divine speech.
The LORD asks Job, “Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth?”—a question highlighting the gap between human knowledge and the secrets of creation.
The founding of the earth is described as an event accompanied by song: the “morning stars” shout for joy, and the “sons of God” rejoice.
The sea is portrayed figuratively as emerging from the womb, as though it were born; in this way, the text presents creation and the appearance of the sea as a controlled process.
The LORD describes the sea as a mighty force but sets a boundary for it: “This far you may come, and no farther.”
Job is asked whether he has ever commanded the morning or caused the dawn to know its place—an illustration of the LORD’s control over the cycles of light and day.
The LORD asks Job whether the “gates of death” and the gates of deep darkness have been revealed to him, presenting the realm of death as a mystery beyond human knowledge.
Snow and hail are described as having “storehouses,” an image that illustrates the LORD’s control over weather phenomena and their availability when needed.
The LORD mentions the Pleiades and Orion and asks whether Job can bind their constellations or loosen their cords—a question about the star systems and the limits of human power.
At the end of the passage, the LORD turns attention to wild animals: Job is asked whether he hunts prey for the lion and satisfies the needs of its young, and who prepares food for the raven’s young.
